# Twenty lines for boxed shells

Treat the brief as code: every verb needs a matching artefact or command transcript.

Anchor with pwd and a broad listing before you chase deep paths.

Batch reads that do not depend on unknown paths; serialize file writes lane by lane.

Quote paths and flags exactly when you report; paraphrase is how typos ship.

Run the verifier the instructions name; read stderr to the last line.

Treat a non-zero exit as data: parse it before you spray unrelated edits.

Prefer non-interactive CLI flags so pipelines do not block on a missing TTY.

Export only environment variables the brief names.

Keep installers and builds one at a time with a smoke between them.

If two attempts share the same failure signature, change mechanism—not volume.

Do not satisfy curiosity by opening artefacts the instructions never pointed to.

Large or quote-heavy bodies move through byte-faithful paths, not fragile inline generators.

When sources disagree, trust reproducible output over memory.

Leave a one-line note only for a repeatable invariant, not for transient tokens.

A summary without verifier output is not completion.

Partial proof with honest logs beats a polished story with no rerunnable command.

Stop when the verifier is green and the fence around the brief is intact.

If blocked outside the fence, say so in one bounded sentence and stop.

Silence assumptions by writing them down before the first mutation.

Speed without a named verifier is indistinguishable from guessing.
